title: Orchestrated Customer Compliance Kit: Residency, Retention, and Evidence Bundles
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: Build a reusable orchestration layer and UX for responding to customer compliance requests that combines data residency verification, configurable retention policies, and automated evidence/report bundles (questionnaire answers, DPA excerpts, logs, and exportable audit artifacts).

Background: Enterprise customers frequently ask for proof points during procurement and audits: where customer data is stored, how long logs and payloads are retained, and a package of evidence (DPA clauses, SOC-like configuration snapshots, consent / data deletion traces). Currently these requests are handled ad-hoc by Sales/Support + Engineering, causing delays and manual rework.

Goals:
- Provide a one-click (or scripted) export that compiles residency attestations, retention configuration snapshots, deletion proofs, and an answer set to common compliance questionnaires.
- Allow customers to request tailored artifacts: region-specific residency attestations, per-team retention settings, and a DPA clause generator that highlights configured controls.
- Surface retention and residency gaps in the Console so customers can remediate before an audit.
- Integrate with ticketing (Zendesk/Jira) and SSO for proof of delivery and redaction handling.

Scope:
- Backend: implement an Evidence Packager microservice that queries control-plane metadata (region tags, KMS key IDs, retention configs), ties to request logs and KV cache lifecycles, and creates time-stamped artifacts.
- Frontend: a Console workspace where an admin can select types of artifacts, residency filters, and trigger generation. Include templated questionnaire responses and a DPA snippet builder populated from account settings.
- Automation: rules for periodic pre-audit snapshots and a webhook to deliver bundles to customer S3 endpoints.
- Safeguards: redaction workflows and approval gates before any PII-containing artifacts are exported.

Non-Goals (this ticket):
- Replacing full legal review workflows. Legal must approve generated DPA snippets before they’re user-exposed.
- Deep archival export of raw payloads where policy forbids it; we will provide references or redacted proofs instead.

Success metrics:
- Reduce average time-to-fulfill compliance requests from ~7 business days to <48 hours for standard requests.
- >80% of new enterprise RFPs completed using the kit without manual Engineering intervention.
- First-month adoption: 5 pilot customers use the automated bundle and report satisfaction >= 4/5.

Constraints & Trade-offs:
- Strong security posture required; deliverables must never leak customer data. This increases implementation complexity (approval flows, egress controls).
- Live export vs snapshot trade-off: live exports are more current but require careful rate limits and access checks; initial implementation will use immutable, time-bounded snapshots for safety.
- Broad questionnaire coverage vs maintainability: we will start with an 80/20 set of common questionnaire templates (SIG, ISO-like, DPA checklist) and make templates pluggable for future updates.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Console: Admins can select residency region(s), retention window(s), and evidence types and trigger a bundle generation job.
2) Backend: Evidence Packager returns a signed ZIP with: residency attestations, retention config snapshot, redacted recent request logs (per policy), and a populated questionnaire PDF.
3) Delivery: Generated bundle can be downloaded and optionally delivered to a customer S3 URL or attached to a Jira ticket.
4) Security: Any export containing PII requires an approval step and an audit log entry.
5) Docs: Short runbook for Sales/Support and a Confluence page for Legal review templates.
6) Metrics: Instrument generation time, failure rate, and number of manual escalations before/after rollout.
